feed.title: For Retirees Who Want Utility Income: Duke Energy vs. Southern Company, 3.9% vs. 3.8% Yield

feed.title: Will Deere's (DE) Shift Toward Construction and Small Equipment Reshape Its Precision Tech Narrative?
feed.summary: Deere's recent performance shows growth in its construction and small equipment units, helping to offset weaker demand in its core agriculture business. This shift is changing the company's revenue mix and could reshape its investment narrative, which has traditionally focused on precision technology and diversification. While this diversification supports the company in the short term, investors still need to monitor cyclical and regional weaknesses in the large agriculture sector, which could impact margins.

feed.title: T-Mobile vs. Verizon: Two Very Different Ways to Own the Same Industry
feed.summary: T-Mobile and Verizon are pursuing contrasting strategies to dominate the telecommunications industry, with T-Mobile focusing on subscriber growth and market share expansion, while Verizon prioritizes income investors with a high dividend yield and a turnaround plan. T-Mobile's strategy has led to significant postpaid service revenue growth, especially with premium plans and expansion into rural markets. Verizon, conversely, has cut subsidies and seen a surge in fiber connections, but its falling ARPA and debt levels mean its turnaround is not yet proven.

feed.title: ADP Warns of Cooling Labor Market While Its Own Business Feels the Chill
feed.summary: ADP's latest figures indicate a significant slowdown in the U.S. labor market, with its "pays per control" growing only 1% in fiscal 2026 and projecting 0-1% for 2027. This cooling trend directly impacts ADP's revenue, as its business model charges per employee paid, and also affects client retention. Despite the slowdown, ADP is leveraging its unique payroll data to offer economic insights and maintain revenue through new business bookings and client float income.

feed.title: Eni (E) and Repsol Explore Partial Divestment of Perla Gas Field Stakes Amid Financing Drive
feed.summary: Eni and Repsol are considering selling parts of their combined 50% stake in Venezuela's Perla natural gas field to secure capital for accelerated development. feed.title: Fortinet Turned $1,000 Into $24,579 in a Decade While the S&P 500 Delivered $3,585
feed.summary: Fortinet (FTNT) saw a $1,000 investment grow to $24,579 in a decade, significantly outperforming the S&P 500's return of $3,585 over the same period, attributed to its strategy of building custom chips and maintaining founder leadership. The company's success is driven by its FortiGate firewall, expansion into cloud-delivered and AI-driven security, and a recent surge in product revenue and billings due to AI workload security upgrades. Despite a high valuation of 63x trailing earnings and cautious analyst ratings, its strong business fundamentals, including a 38% non-GAAP operating margin and consistent EPS beats, suggest continued growth, though the stock's recent doubling already reflects much of this performance.
